solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get down with His Majesty? That's a sore point

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, King Charles
what you cry when a sore point is touched

explanation.surface: Someone is told to kneel before the King, then complains about a painful spot.
explanation.walkthrough: CR (Carolus Rex) is the cipher of King Charles, so His Majesty today.
explanation.definitionFit: To crouch is to bend low, a verb synonym for getting down close to the ground.

clue.text: Risky holding royal personage in court

indicators.note: one word holding another keeps it inside its own letters

parts.note: chancy means uncertain or dangerous
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A risky business involving a royal figure ending up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal personage is the crossword standby for the late Queen, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery is a division of the English High Court, historically the Lord Chancellor's court of equity.

clue.text: Bill can be so wonderful!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an unpaid bill is still owed

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at what a bill might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation sounds like praise for a bill, but the first meaning is the dull one: not yet paid.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both unpaid and still due, and excellent or remarkable in quality.

clue.text: American leaving drink, the clown

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a hot chocolate drink
A is the usual abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American abandons his drink and becomes a circus clown.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the final A from COCOA. Coco the Clown was a famous circus clown in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Coco the Clown, stage name of Nicolai Poliakoff, was the best-known circus clown in mid-century Britain.

clue.text: I bad-mouth a Cypriot maybe

parts.note: taken as written
to slander is to speak ill of someone

explanation.surface: A speaker confesses to speaking ill of someone from Cyprus.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is an island, so a Cypriot is one example of an island inhabitant.

clue.text: Second nuclear missile demanding attention

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
Trident is the UK's submarine-launched nuclear missile system

explanation.surface: A second nuclear weapon is the sort of thing that grabs headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice or argument is loud and harsh, forcing people to notice it.

clue.text: A department head covering up department's conduct

parts.note: taken as written
D is an abbreviation for department
a government minister heads a department

explanation.surface: A senior official hides how his department behaves.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry the department head sits below D, so it is covered up by it; the letters run A, D, then the minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer is to manage or run affairs, a verb synonym for conduct as in conducting business.

clue.text: Old man having heart transplant? It won't work

indicators.note: a transplant swaps one organ for another, so the central letter is replaced

parts.note: old man is slang for father

explanation.surface: An elderly man undergoes heart surgery that may not succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The A at the centre of DAD is swapped for U, the only letter that makes a word meaning a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud is a thing that fails to function, like a shell that does not explode.

clue.text: Break promise, trapped by Chinese general on way north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading from the bottom up
letters trapped by the following words sit inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and most of the second

explanation.surface: A general in China breaks his word and is caught heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across chinESE GENERal, read upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise or commitment, so it is the verb for breaking one.

clue.text: Two males, one with no need for Viagra?

definitions.text: one with no need for Viagra?

parts.note: a he is a male
a man is a male

explanation.surface: A cheeky joke about a virile man who needs no pills.
explanation.walkthrough: Two males gives two words for a male, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A he-man is a strongly masculine, virile man, the type joked to need no help from Viagra.

clue.text: It could be an opinion piece in the Guardian?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a piece of writing in a newspaper

definitions.note: an example of the answer, hence the 'It could be' and the question mark
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word 'the' is the definite one in grammar

explanation.surface: A newspaper column in the Guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'the' of 'the Guardian' is a definite article, giving the answer its second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a written newspaper piece and also the grammar term for words like 'the' and 'a'.

clue.text: Hurried to grab first man, running back fast

indicators.note: to grab something is to hold it within, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: ran means hurried

indicators.note: running back means going in the opposite direction, so read the name backwards

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to catch the first man as he sprints back.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast looks like an adjective tied to running, but it is a noun: a period without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic month of fasting, so it names a fast.

clue.text: Praise faculty in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as it is said, not as it is written

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses or faculties

explanation.surface: Commending a university department in an address.
explanation.walkthrough: Faculty looks academic here but means a sense, such as sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite someone is to commend them officially, as in a mention in dispatches, so it means praise.

clue.text: Pal thus making erotic entertainment?

parts.note: surface reading: a friend creating something
setter's reading: the letters of pal shuffled around, as if moving to music, give another three-letter word, and the answer describes that

explanation.surface: A friend producing an adult show.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as instructions, turns pal into its rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Lap dancing is a strip-club act where a dancer performs close to a seated customer, an erotic entertainment.

clue.text: Predictable condition of Iberian into rum

indicators.note: rum here means odd or strange, so the letters are put into a strange order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spaniard who takes to rum ends up in the expected state.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is a drink in the picture but an anagram signal in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Inebriation is drunkenness, the state you would predict for someone keen on rum.

clue.text: Individual in residence breaking court order

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it apart so its letters can be reassembled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single individual
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone breaks into a house and breaches a court order.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree nisi is a provisional court order in English divorce proceedings.

clue.text: Park employee, new arrival losing way

indicators.note: losing something means letting go of it, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a stranger is someone newly arrived in a place
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A new park employee gets lost on his way.
explanation.definitionFit: A park ranger is employed to look after a national or country park.

clue.text: Worried you might find Rosemary here?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the herb rosemary goes into a casserole

explanation.surface: Wondering if a woman named Rosemary might be found in a fretful state.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Rosemary look like a woman's name; it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being anxious, and literally where a cook puts a herb such as rosemary.

clue.text: Too inept to move stealthily

indicators.note: letters made to move change their places in the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone too clumsy to sneak about quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To move stealthily' reads as one phrase, but the split comes after move.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking on tiptoe keeps footsteps quiet, so the phrase describes moving stealthily.

clue.text: Senior officer supports head of state on Panama, perhaps

parts.note: bras are supporting garments

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of state
a Panama is a straw hat

explanation.surface: A senior officer backs a Latin American head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Panama looks like the country; it is the straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass hat is British military slang for a high-ranking officer, from the gold braid on their caps.

clue.text: Cambridge University admitting old lady, an expatriate

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the Massachusetts Institute of Technology is in Cambridge, Massachusetts
a grandmother

explanation.surface: A Cambridge college admits an elderly woman from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge points to the English city, but the university is the American one.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant is a person who has moved to another country, broadly an expatriate.

clue.text: Mistake by model, troublesome youngster

parts.note: the Model T Ford
a mistake

explanation.surface: A modelling slip-up by an unruly child.
explanation.walkthrough: The model is the Model T car, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A little terror is an informal name for a naughty, unruly child.

clue.text: Capital of country held by army once

indicators.note: something held by another is enclosed in its grip

parts.note: the Territorial Army, renamed the Army Reserve in 2014
a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A capital city once under military occupation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's volunteer reserve force until its renaming, hence once.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirana is the capital city of Albania.

clue.text: Ridiculous episode beginning and ending like this

parts.words: episode beginning and ending like this
parts.note: surface reading: a silly episode from start to finish
setter's reading: the word episode starts and finishes with the same vowel, and the answer, split into three short words, describes that

explanation.surface: A silly episode that is absurd from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN AN E: episode begins and ends that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and lacking sense, a synonym for ridiculous.

clue.text: Constituent and I get dinner out

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order or disarranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook announcing they will serve dinner and its components.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is one component part of a mixture or recipe.

clue.text: Long time spent in a stupor, might one say?

indicators.note: what one might say is how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: to be in a daze is to be in a stunned, confused state

explanation.surface: Wondering how long someone has spent dazed.
explanation.definitionFit: Days, as in 'it took days', is an informal way of saying a long period.

clue.text: Lake where vicar's lost in daydream

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a reverie is a daydream
Rev, Reverend, the title of a vicar

explanation.surface: A lakeside spot where a clergyman drifts into a daydream.
explanation.definitionFit: Erie is one of the five Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: First articles set before a non-believer

parts.note: two articles, a and the
1st, written with the numeral as I

explanation.surface: Instructions to place the leading pieces in front of an unbeliever.
explanation.walkthrough: 1st is the ordinal, with the 1 taken as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist is a person who does not believe in any god.

clue.text: Enjoys shiatsu every now and then

indicators.note: every now and then means at intervals, so only every other letter is used

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone who likes a Japanese massage from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Shiatsu is a Japanese pressure-point massage.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something can mean to enjoy it, as in has a good time or enjoys good health.

clue.text: New queen a cracker — but a little obsessive?

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
ER, Elizabeth Regina
a cracker and a dish are both slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A new queen is a stunner, yet slightly fixated.
explanation.walkthrough: Cracker is British slang for something excellent or a good-looking person, as is dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerdish describes someone slightly geeky, with a narrow, intense, rather obsessive interest.

clue.text: A seaman said to be the mugger?

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the sound of the words matters

parts.note: a seaman is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is accused of being the attacker.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailer is one who attacks, which is what a mugger does to a victim.

clue.text: Seed of a never-ending comic strip?

indicators.note: never-ending means without an end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: Charles Schulz's comic strip featuring Snoopy and Charlie Brown

explanation.surface: Wondering about the origins of a long-running cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Peanuts ran for nearly fifty years, adding to the never-ending joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is the edible seed of a legume plant, grown underground.
